purpose: Bismuth subsalicylate is used to treat upset stomach, heartburn, nausea, indigestion, and diarrhea. It can also help with traveler's diarrhea. Many people reach for it when their stomach just feels off or they have loose stools.
how_it_works: This medication works in a few ways to calm your digestive system. It coats the lining of your stomach and intestines to protect them from irritation. It also has mild antibacterial properties that help fight certain germs that can cause stomach upset and diarrhea.
common_side_effects: The most noticeable side effect is that your tongue and stools may turn black or dark gray — this is completely harmless and temporary, so don't be alarmed! You may also notice your stools become darker in color. Some people experience mild constipation.
warnings: Do not give this medication to children or teenagers who have or are recovering from chickenpox or the flu, as it contains salicylate (similar to aspirin) and can cause a rare but serious condition called Reye's syndrome. If you are allergic to aspirin, avoid this medication. Talk to your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking blood thinners, as this medication may interact with them. Do not use for more than 2 days without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: For adults and teens 12 and older, the usual dose is 2 tablets or 30 mL (about 2 tablespoons) of liquid every 30 minutes to 1 hour as needed, but do not take more than 8 doses in 24 hours. Always follow the directions on the package or as told by your doctor or pharmacist.
